messages:
incident-bot: ALERT → Sev2: sustained high p95 latency on /v1/generate (us-west-2). Trigger: latency > 1.2s for 15m. Paging @Alex (oncall).
Alex (oncall): got it, joining. checking dashboards now...
Alex (oncall): p95 ~1.35s, throughput steady, error rate normal. KV cache hit rate dropped ~20% on a subset of pods.
Maya (sre): noted. any recent deploys? rolling restart earlier at 23:40 UTC.
Jordan (eng-ops): confirmed rolling restart for rollout v2.13. Might be related to kernel flags on that cluster.
Alex (oncall): I'm going to route small models for interactive traffic and scale up capacity 2x in us-west-2. @Jordan please prepare routing change and scale command.
Jordan (eng-ops): running: `infra scale --pool infer-usw2 --count +2` — starting now.
Jordan (eng-ops): routing change: applying adaptive routing to prefer model-quant-s1 for requests with short context. CMD: ```/api/routing/set?policy=latency_prefer_quant``` — rolling.
Lina (product): what's customer impact? do we need a status page blurb?
Ryan (CS): I've got two enterprise customers on us-west-2. They might see increased latency for long-context requests. We should notify depending on ETA.
Alex (oncall): estimated recovery 12-18 minutes after scale completes. I'll draft a short status page update.
Alex (oncall): STATUS PAGE DRAFT: "We are experiencing elevated latency for text generation in our US-West region. Engineers are scaling capacity and applying adaptive routing to reduce impact. Customers may see slower responses for large-context requests. Next update in 15 minutes." :hourglass_flowing_sand: 
Maya (sre): add note re: mitigation: fallback to quantized model for short queries. That reduces latency but may slightly change tokenization/formatting.
Lina (product): customer notification (short): "We're investigating increased generation latency in US-West impacting long-context requests. We're scaling capacity and routing short requests to a lower-latency model. No data loss. We'll update within 30 minutes"
Ryan (CS): okay I'll send that to the two impacted accounts and offer a status webhook. Draft DM: "Hi — we're seeing elevated generation latency in US-West impacting longer prompts. We're actively mitigating via capacity scale and routing; you may see degraded p95 for long requests. ETA ~15-30m. Reach out if this affects production traffic." Should I send?
Jordan (eng-ops): scale finished. New nodes healthy. Metrics show p95 dropping to 0.9s on many pods. Still some pods at 1.1s due to cache warmup.
Alex (oncall): good. keep monitoring. if p95 doesn't drop below 1s in 10m, we'll force KV cache warmup: `curl -XPOST https://infra/ops/warmup_cache --region=us-west-2`
Maya (sre): FYI I can take the post-scale follow-up for 30m, then hand back to Alex.
Alex (oncall): noted — I'll stay on for next update. Ops, please confirm status page publish.
Jordan (eng-ops): published status page update (draft) and set visibility to customers subscribed to US-West. URL: https://status.redwood.ai/incidents/3251112222
incident-bot: Incident status changed → Mitigating. Updates every 15m.
Alex (oncall): Last note: postmortem owners: Alex + Jordan + Maya. Root cause TBD (cache invalidation + rollout timing). Will collate logs.
Ryan (CS): Sent customer messages to impacted accounts and created follow-up ticket.
Lina (product): OK. I'll prepare external advisory if recovery >1h. For now status page and targeted DMs.
Alex (oncall): thanks all. next update in 15m. :white_check_mark:
